channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Eleição já sofre cerco dos EUA, resta saber alcance da mão peluda de Trump
item.description: US interference in Brazil's 2026 elections is no longer a backstage hypothesis but a consolidated fact, which should worry democrats regardless of partisan preference. The electoral landscape is being shaped by external forces, especially those linked to influencer Trump, threatening the autonomy of the Brazilian democratic process.

item.title: Lula e Janja vão a SC pela 1ª vez na campanha e buscam voto feminino
item.description: Lula and Janja visit Santa Catarina for the first time in the campaign, delivering a speech against femicide and calling for women to vote. In 2022, the state was a stronghold of support for Jair Bolsonaro, who received 69.2% of the votes.

item.title: Lula repete que, se depender de sua vontade, acabará com as bets no Brasil
item.description: President Lula stated during a campaign event in Santa Catarina that he intends to ban online betting (bets) in Brazil, arguing that these practices benefit only a small group at the expense of society.

item.title: 'Quer comprar voto dos pobres', diz Flávio sobre reajuste do Bolsa Família
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro accuses Lula of trying to buy votes from the poor with a Bolsa Família adjustment announced 17 days before elections, calling the current president's actions 'desperation'. The PL candidate mocked the government announcement, suggesting it is an electoral strategy. The statement comes at a time of intensification of the presidential campaign.

item.title: Em SC, Lula reforça que vai acabar com as bets
item.description: President Lula stated in Florianópolis his intention to ban electronic betting (bets) in Brazil, arguing they lead to debt and damage family relationships. He dismissed football clubs' criticism, noting teams won titles without the betting market.

item.title: Dirigente de ONG com recursos federais lidera movimento pró-Lula
item.description: João Paulo Mehl, an NGO leader with federal funding, heads the Pro-Lula Cultural Movement, which supports Lula's re-election without being part of the official campaign. First Lady Janja participated in a virtual event where attendees called for votes for the president and criticized the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Guerra entre 'dinistas' no Maranhão reacende debate sobre atuação política de Dino como juiz
item.description: The political dispute in Maranhão involving 'Dino supporters' reignites debates about Flávio Dino's performance as a judge and his political past. In 2023, Dino stated in a Senate hearing that he would leave political life if approved for the Supreme Court, but discussions about his influence persist.

item.title: Michelle e Damares gravam campanha de apresentador condenado por homofobia
item.description: Presenter Sikêra Jr., convicted of homophobia, recorded campaign materials with Michelle Bolsonaro and Damares Alves for his bid for the Chamber of Deputies in São Paulo. He acknowledged his mistake, reaffirmed respect for the LGBTQIA+ community, and condemned any form of discrimination. The supporting videos will air on Saturday (September 19th).

item.title: Em carreata, Sebastião Coelho critica postura do STF: "Desordem judicial"
item.description: Sebastião Coelho, candidate to the Senate by the New Party, held a caravan in Núcleo Bandeirante supported by volunteers who paid their own expenses. During the event, he criticized the STF, accusing the judiciary of disorder, and emphasized that the campaign is driven by citizens without public funding.

item.title: Lula volta a prometer fim das bets e dispara contra times patrocinados por apostas
item.description: In a speech in Florianópolis, President Lula promised to ban online betting houses in Brazil, rejecting the argument from football clubs that the market is essential for sports. He joked that clubs claim his policy will end football and pointed out that no major titles have been won since betting became widespread. Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro held a campaign rally in Joinville.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que SP não quer eleger senadores de esquerda e vê com otimismo vitória de Flávio
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated that the state does not want to elect left-wing senators and publicly supported candidates André do Prado and Guilherme Derrite. He expressed optimism about Flávio Bolsonaro's victory and announced R$25 billion in investments for climate adaptation and resilience if reelected. The campaign aims to expand its voter base in areas where Tarcísio performed worse in 2022.

item.title: Regra eleitoral restringe prisão de candidatos a partir deste sábado e é válida até 48 horas depois do primeiro turno; veja como funciona
item.description: Starting Saturday, candidates in the 2026 elections cannot be arrested or detained, except in cases of flagrante delito, as provided in Article 236 of the Electoral Code. The restriction applies until 48 hours after the first round and is reactivated for the second round. The measure aims to prevent arrests from interfering with the electoral dispute, without affecting investigations or proceedings.

item.title: Seleção masculina de vôlei vence a Venezuela e decidirá vaga nas Olimpíadas contra a Argentina
item.description: The Brazilian volleyball team defeated Venezuela 3-0 and now faces Argentina in the final match of the South American Championship for the Olympic spot. Maintaining a perfect record, Brazil seeks to reaffirm its continental dominance against a longtime rival.

item.title: Janja convoca mulheres a buscar votos para Lula em SC
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula called on women to campaign for President Lula's reelection in Santa Catarina, highlighting policies like reduced work hours and elimination of the 6X1 shift schedule. Speaking in Florianópolis, she urged a non-confrontational approach to wavering and former Bolsonarist voters, mentioning initiatives such as the Popular Pharmacy and tax increases for the wealthy.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro e outros candidatos de direita usam foto de Gonet para atacar Lula e STF
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet became a target of Bolsonarist criticism after a photo of him smoking a cigar and drinking whiskey with former banker Daniel Vorcaro spread on social media. Under investigation for alleged donation requests, Gonet is cited by Flávio Bolsonaro to attack the Lula government and the STF.

item.title: Durigan defende reajuste do Bolsa Família às vésperas da eleição: ‘Foi pela inflação, não foi real’
item.description: Finance Minister Durigan defended the 15% increase in Bolsa Família, stating it follows inflation and does not represent real spending growth. Despite the estimated impact of R$ 5.8 billion in 2026, the government reaffirms its commitment to improving public accounts, while critics point to worsening deficits and accusations of judicial maneuvering in the STF.

item.title: OpenAI diz que Brasil é teste global para IA nas eleições
item.description: OpenAI described Brazil as a global testbed for AI use in elections, emphasizing TSE rules and the need to prevent model bias. The company highlighted tools to identify AI-generated content and the significance of AI-specific regulation ahead of the 2026 election cycle.

item.title: Quase 4 milhões de pequenos negócios já foram abertos em 2026
item.description: Entrepreneurship in Brazil grew 14.3% between January and August 2026, with 3.93 million new small businesses opened. Sebrae highlighted Amapá as the leader in percentage growth (+34.1%) and São Paulo as the largest source of new companies in absolute numbers (1.16 million). Individual micro-entrepreneurs accounted for 77% of new CNPJs in the period.

item.title: Três Poderes: Cármen Lúcia é a vencedora da semana e Milton Leite, o perdedor
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia was highlighted for apologizing to Brazilian society for the confusion during the session discussing the banker Daniel Vorcaro's ties with court members. Justice Milton Leite was deemed the week's loser for his stance during the same event.

item.title: Candidato usa Bolsonaro em santinho apesar de veto do TSE
item.description: State representative Gil Diniz (PL-SP), running for Congress, distributes campaign flyers featuring Jair Bolsonaro, defying a TSE ruling banning the use of the former president's image in campaigns. Minister Estela Aranha had previously barred Lucas Bove's campaign from using Bolsonaro's photos.

item.title: Paes elogia plano integrado de segurança e admite fazer pouca campanha na capital
item.description: Eduardo Paes praised the integrated security plan announced by Lula and Couto, emphasizing cooperation between federal, state, and municipal governments. He supports the Fluminense Security System and admits to campaigning little in the capital. During a walk in Madureira, he was accompanied by allies and coalition candidates, while some remained neutral in the gubernatorial race.

item.title: Oposição cobra afastamento de Gonet após foto com Vorcaro em Londres
item.description: Opposition leaders demanded the removal of Attorney General Paulo Gonet after a photo surfaced showing him with banker Daniel Vorcaro in London. Gonet denied any close ties to Vorcaro at the Supreme Court, but opponents accuse him of lying. The meeting allegedly occurred in 2024.

item.title: Telegram detalha plano contra desinformação nas eleições de 2026
item.description: Telegram submitted a compliance plan to the TSE for the 2026 elections, outlining measures to prevent misinformation, illegal content, and fake identities. The platform emphasized content moderation of public groups and channels, strengthened data protection protocols, and automated channels for privacy-related requests. Private communications will remain unmonitored.

item.title: Renan Santos quer usar FGTS na aposentadoria, diz Kim Kataguiri
item.description: Renan Santos proposes using the FGTS balance as capitalization for retirement within a three-pillar pension reform: minimum income, pay-as-you-go, and capitalization. Kim Kataguiri also supports reviewing R$200 billion/year in tax benefits and phasing out the Manaus Free Trade Zone.

item.title: Botafogo inicia era Tite contra o Mirassol em busca de estabilidade no Brasileirão
item.description: Botafogo kicks off the Tite era against Mirassol in the Brasileirão, seeking stability after the win over Grêmio. The team aims to increase its lead over the relegation zone and close the gap to Fluminense. Tite emphasized the importance of securing points before the FIFA break, looking ahead to upcoming matches.

item.title: A disputa entre Tarcísio e Haddad nas redes sociais
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas leads the São Paulo polls with 49%, ahead of Fernando Haddad at 29%, boosting more social media posts and spending BRL 1.4 million on ads, emphasizing public safety and governance. Haddad, spending BRL 1.1 million, focuses on defending his image amid scandals such as the Banco Master case.

item.title: Como o PT tenta reescrever um slogan bolsonarista para a campanha de Lula
item.description: The PT reworked the Bolsonaro slogan during the 2026 campaign by flipping the phrase 'whoever votes for Lula votes for Moraes' to 'whoever votes for Flávio Bolsonaro votes for Daniel Vorcaro,' amid electoral debates centered on corruption accusations and the Supreme Court's political influence. This strategy aims to shift the narrative away from alleged election fraud and target Flávio Bolsonaro's involvement in the Banco Master scandal.

item.title: 38% veem Lula prejudicado pela crise no STF; 31% citam Flávio
item.description: A September 2026 Datafolha poll shows 38% of respondents believe Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) is the presidential candidate most harmed by the STF and Banco Master crisis, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 31%. The crisis is expected to influence voting decisions, according to 47% of respondents.

item.title: Enganação até o 1° turno: como Flávio tenta driblar as investigações
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces new setback after revelations about his relationship with lawyer Willer Tomaz, investigated in the INSS fraud scheme, involving a safari in South Africa, private jet flights and use of an apartment coveted by Daniel Vorcaro's nephew.

item.title: As desculpas de Cármen Lúcia
item.description: Justice Carmen Lucia apologized to Brazilian society for not helping calm tensions at the Supreme Court during a controversial session. The author criticizes the lack of ethical consensus in Brazil and points to the Supreme Court as a power without checks and balances, citing international accountability cases. The text highlights polarization around Alexandre de Moraes and the absence of concrete ethical sanctions in Brazil.

item.title: TSE suspende regra e presos provisórios poderão votar em 2026
item.description: The TSE (Superior Electoral Court) decided to suspend the voting ban for pretrial detainees established by the Anti-Fraud Law, allowing them to vote in the 2026 elections, although in smaller numbers due to bureaucratic restrictions. The decision is based on the principle of electoral annuuality, which prevents legislative changes less than one year before the election.

item.title: Lula: “Votar nas mulheres de direita não dá certo”
item.description: President Lula stated during a rally in Guarulhos that voting for right-wing women does not work, advocating support for left-wing candidates such as Marina Silva and Simone Tebet for the Senate in São Paulo. His remark sparked mixed reactions, standing out in the gender and partisan debate within the Brazilian electoral landscape of 2026.

item.title: ‘Sonso’, ‘mentiroso’ e ‘cara de pau’: Gonet é alvo de críticas após foto com Vorcaro
item.description: A photo of the Attorney General, Paulo Gonet, with banker Daniel Vorcaro in London sparked criticism from politicians who questioned the alleged lack of connection between the two. Gonet had previously denied, during a STF session, having any closeness to Vorcaro. Lawmakers like Nikolas Ferreira and Romeu Zema labeled the prosecutor as 'liar' and 'tedious', intensifying the debate on ethics and public image of authorities.

item.title: Ala do PL diz que agenda do vice de Flávio foi suspensa por falta de quórum
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar (PL), running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro, had his campaign event suspended in Irecê (BA), with organizers citing Anac's recommendation about aerodrome conditions, while a PL faction blamed low turnout and mobilization challenges. The event followed Flávio's campaign activities in Vitória da Conquista.

item.title: Rui Costa Pimenta quer ampliar direitos trabalhistas e verbas da saúde
item.description: Rui Costa Pimenta, PCO candidate for president, proposes expanding labor rights and investing in public health with more funding, hospital construction, and professional hiring. His proposals include public education nationalization, expropriation of vacant properties, land reform, and salary increases. He advocates progressive policies such as opening medical schools without entrance exams and demarcating indigenous lands.

item.title: Caiado promete governo "transformador" e reformas estruturais
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD presidential candidate, proposes a 'transformative' government focused on security, fiscal responsibility, and productive growth. He advocates for harsher penalties, a new public security ministry, and inter-branch cooperation to pass structural reforms.

item.title: A nova pesquisa Datafolha sobre a disputa Lula x Flávio no maior colégio eleitoral do Brasil
item.description: A new Datafolha poll, registered as BR-09355/2026 and conducted between September 22 and 24, 2026, examines the 2026 electoral race in São Paulo, covering presidential, state, and senatorial contests. The survey tests thirteen first-round presidential candidates, including Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado, along with five second-round scenarios, emphasizing the Lula versus Flávio matchup. The poll also includes a section on the Supreme Federal Court's performance, addressing ethics, suspicions in the Banco Master case, and the court's influence on candidate campaigns. The survey includes 1.610 interviews with a ±2-point margin of error, scheduled for release on September 24.

item.title: Abin alerta governo Lula sobre interferência "crítica" dos EUA nas eleições
item.description: The Abin warned the Lula government about risks of US electoral interference in 2026, highlighting geopolitical pressures and sanctions linked to figures like Eduardo Bolsonaro. The report indicates the Trump administration prioritizes regional control and views Brazil as an obstacle to US influence in Latin America.

item.title: Facções ou 8/1: Lula contesta Trump e liga terrorismo a Bolsonaro
item.description: On the Noblat program, Lula criticized Trump and linked Bolsonaro to state terrorism, referencing the January 8th coup plots. The parliamentary caucus discussed the risk of a Flávio Bolsonaro government with a seven-vote majority in the Supreme Court, with appointments of up to five ministers.

item.title: Lula na defensiva, Flávio no ataque: como a crise no STF já afeta as campanhas eleitorais
item.description: The STF crisis, marked by corruption suspicions involving justices and former banker Daniel Vorcaro, is directly influencing the 2026 election campaign, putting Lula on the defensive and Flávio Bolsonaro on the attack. The presidential race has lost focus on issues like economy, health, and public security, with 7% of voters undecided after PF revelations.

item.title: Renan propõe cortes na Previdência e alterar pisos da saúde e educação
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate from the Missão party, proposes pension cuts, unlinks health and education floors from RCL, and replaces Bolsa Família with Citizen Fronts. His plan includes a fiscal adjustment of R$1.1 trillion by 2031, federal oversight of inefficient municipalities, and doubled infrastructure investments.

item.title: Norte é pouco representado em pesquisas eleitorais, diz especialista
item.description: Political scientist Naiara Alcantara pointed out the underrepresentation of Northern Brazilian voters in electoral polls, noting the scarcity of research companies in the region. She analyzed the tension between economic development and environmental preservation, especially regarding oil exploration in the Equatorial Margin, and stressed that environmental concern does not necessarily translate into electoral choices. Alcantara also highlighted Lula's strength among Northern voters, attributing it to the socioeconomic profile and the presence of social public policies.

item.title: Nova Paraná Pesquisas mostra Zucco e Juliana Brizola na disputa pela liderança no RS
item.description: A new survey by Paraná Pesquisas shows federal deputy Luciano Zucco (PL) leading the race for governor of Rio Grande do Sul with 36.4% of voting intentions, followed by Juliana Brizola (PDT) with 31.3%. The Senate race indicates Manuela D'Ávila (PSOL) in the lead with 32.2% of voting intentions.

item.title: Caminhos para o STF recuperar a imagem
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court of Brazil faces a deepening institutional credibility crisis, exacerbated by postponed rulings and internal disputes among justices, particularly regarding Alexandre de Moraes. Legal scholars emphasize the need for cultural reforms within the Court, including term limits and greater transparency. The ongoing crisis affects other institutions such as the Federal Police and the Senate, which closely watch the Court's developments.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Lula states that, if it depends on his personal will, he will end online betting in the country, viewing it as a vice and a disease, and that the government must prioritize protecting the lives of citizens, especially the poor, rather than focusing solely on tax collection.

item.title: O prazo de Lula para bater o martelo sobre a medida anti-bets
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva intends to issue a provisional measure to restrict online betting, particularly the so-called 'Tigrinho games', before the first round of elections on October 4. The initiative, to be discussed with ministers after returning from the UN, faces internal government division, with the economic team showing resistance. Lula supports the measure to protect young people, citing football champions who won titles without betting.

item.title: Filho de Covas declara apoio a Lula e diz que Flávio é muito pior que o pai
item.description: Mário Covas Neto, former São Paulo city councilor and son of Governor Mário Covas, endorsed Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) for the 2026 presidential race, following alignment with Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), who was also his father's running mate. In press statements, Zuzinha asserted that Senator Flávio Dino (PSB) is far worse than his father, Mário Covas, but emphasized that Lula represents a more viable alternative for Brazil.

item.title: Dono de ONG bancada pelo governo mobiliza campanha paralela de Lula com aval de Janja
item.description: The owner of an NGO that received R$5.6 million from the federal government leads a parallel campaign supporting Lula's reelection, using resources from Ministry of Culture civil servants and involving members of the Culture Points, without registering the actions and profiles used with the TSE.

item.title: Campanha de Lula estimula ‘missões’ diárias para militância reagir à alta de Flávio nas pesquisas
item.description: Lula's campaign launched a daily grassroots mobilization effort on social media to promote government achievements and attack Flávio Bolsonaro and Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça, amid a technical tie and Flávio's recent lead in polls. Daily 'missions' are sent via WhatsApp, encouraging sharing and conversations with undecided voters, particularly focused on reinforcing the Bolsa Família program.

item.title: Aliados tentam convencer Flávio a ir a NY entre o 1º e 2º turnos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) allies push for a New York trip between the first and second rounds of the 2026 elections to meet investors, but the senator prefers to stay in Brazil due to the short 20-day campaign window. The plan aims to strengthen his profile with international financial markets.
